entries.title: Basic Anatomy Review

testable_competencies.anatomy_overview: Recognize normal pelvic/reproductive anatomy as background for the menstrual, infection, prolapse, and oncology units that follow.

entries.zero_question_reason: Normal anatomy background, not independently testable; frames the condition-specific units later in the chapter.

entries.title: Menstrual Cycle Physiology

testable_competencies.cycle_physiology: Recognize the normal hormonal phases of the menstrual cycle (follicular, ovulatory, luteal) as background for amenorrhea, AUB, PMS/PMDD, and infertility units.

entries.zero_question_reason: Normal physiology background; not independently testable but underlies several downstream condition-specific units.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 112 requires the candidate to diagnose cause, severity and complications and initiate management for abnormal vaginal bleeding, which in practice requires ordering the pelvic imaging and/or endometrial biopsy this unit covers as the investigative step; the objective's text does not itself name the specific investigations.

testable_competencies.investigation_selection: Select appropriate first-line imaging (pelvic ultrasound) and endometrial sampling for a patient with suspected structural or endometrial pathology, e.g. abnormal uterine bleeding.

entries.title: Hysterectomy

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective addresses hysterectomy indications/complications directly; objective 112's management step for refractory abnormal uterine bleeding is the nearest adjacent evidence for when hysterectomy becomes an appropriate next step.

testable_competencies.indications_and_complications: Recognize the major indications (e.g., refractory AUB, symptomatic fibroids, malignancy, prolapse) and major complications for hysterectomy at a level sufficient to counsel and refer a patient appropriately.

do_not_test: Operative technique/surgical approach detail (abdominal vs. vaginal vs. laparoscopic route selection, intraoperative steps) - specialist-level detail beyond generalist decision value.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 56-1 is an exact match: 'the candidate will complete a relevant history and physical examination... In particular, the candidate will first rule out pregnancy. In amenorrhea, the candidate will then differentiate between primary and secondary.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Rule out pregnancy first, then differentiate primary from secondary amenorrhea and characterize oligomenorrhea, identifying the compartment-based (hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian-uterine/outflow) cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 112 is an exact match: 'Given a patient who presents with excessive, irregular, and/or abnormal vaginal bleeding, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications, and initiate an appropriate management plan.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_workup: Diagnose the cause of abnormal uterine bleeding (structural vs. non-structural, e.g. PALM-COEIN framework) across the reproductive lifespan (adolescent, reproductive-age, perimenopausal, postmenopausal) and initiate appropriate investigation.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate management plan and recognize when bleeding severity requires urgent intervention.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 56-2 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with dysmenorrhea, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications... Specifically, the candidate will differentiate primary from secondary dysmenorrhea.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate primary from secondary dysmenorrhea and recognize secondary causes (e.g., endometriosis, adenomyosis, fibroids) requiring further workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 73 requires diagnosing the cause, severity, and complications of pelvic pain in a female patient; endometriosis is a leading cause of chronic pelvic pain but is not named explicitly in the retrieved objective text, so this is treated as the general presentation this unit's diagnosis feeds into rather than a name-specific match.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 56-2 requires differentiating primary from secondary dysmenorrhea; endometriosis is a leading secondary cause, making this unit's diagnosis a direct input to that differentiation even though endometriosis is not named in the objective text.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize endometriosis as a cause of chronic pelvic pain, secondary dysmenorrhea, and infertility, and identify the pattern of clinical features suggesting the diagnosis.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate initial management plan (e.g., hormonal suppression) and recognize indications for referral (e.g., infertility, refractory pain, suspected deep infiltrating disease).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Adenomyosis is a structural cause of heavy/abnormal uterine bleeding covered by objective 112's differential, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Adenomyosis is a recognized secondary cause of dysmenorrhea under objective 56-2's differentiation requirement, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize adenomyosis as a cause of heavy menstrual bleeding and secondary dysmenorrhea, typically in a parous patient with a diffusely enlarged, tender uterus, and distinguish it from fibroids and endometriosis on clinical grounds.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 17 is an exact match: 'Given a patient who presents with a need or request for contraception, the candidate will discuss the available treatment options and initiate an appropriate management plan.'

testable_competencies.method_counselling: Discuss and select among hormonal methods, intrauterine devices, and emergency postcoital contraception based on patient preference, contraindications, and efficacy.
testable_competencies.emergency_contraception: Recognize indications and time-sensitive window for emergency postcoital contraception.

entries.title: Termination of Pregnancy

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 121-1 requires the candidate to 'take the necessary steps to obtain valid legal and ethical consent for the proposed action, taking into account issues related to decision-making capacity, information sharing, the form of consent, limitations, and exceptions' - directly applicable to counselling a patient requesting termination of pregnancy, though the objective is general-consent framed rather than abortion-specific.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 81's management-plan and supportive-counselling requirements are the nearest analog for structured pregnancy-outcome counselling, but its title and rationale are scoped to spontaneous/threatened loss rather than induced/elective termination.

testable_competencies.counselling_and_referral: Counsel a patient requesting termination of pregnancy on available options (medical vs. surgical), obtain appropriate informed consent, and initiate referral within the applicable gestational-age and access framework.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Abortion is federally decriminalized in Canada but gestational-age limits, funding, and service access vary provincially/territorially; ELOM may separately cover the underlying consent/capacity framework in more general terms - PRIMARY_OWNER not finalized here, recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

entries.title: Early Pregnancy Loss and First-Trimester Bleeding

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 81 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with a threatened abortion, the candidate will clarify the status of the pregnancy, identify any complications, and initiate an appropriate management plan. Particular attention should be paid to supportive counselling of parents and to appropriate investigation in cases of recurrent spontaneous abortion.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Evaluate first-trimester bleeding to determine pregnancy viability and classify the type of spontaneous abortion (threatened, inevitable, incomplete, complete, missed).
testable_competencies.management: Initiate appropriate management (expectant, medical, or surgical) and provide supportive counselling; investigate recurrent pregnancy loss.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for ectopic pregnancy specifically; objective 81's 'clarify the status of the pregnancy' requirement for a patient with early bleeding/threatened abortion is the closest adjacent evidence, since ectopic pregnancy is a critical differential diagnosis for exactly that presentation, though the objective's own title and rationale describe spontaneous/threatened loss rather than ectopic implantation.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_urgency: Recognize ectopic pregnancy as a life-threatening cause of early pregnancy bleeding/pain, identify risk factors, and initiate urgent investigation (beta-hCG trend, transvaginal ultrasound) and management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 46 is an exact match: 'Given a couple with infertility, the candidate will diagnose the cause and will explain the therapeutic options.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose female-factor (ovulatory, tubal, uterine) and male-factor causes of infertility in a couple.
testable_competencies.counselling: Explain the range of therapeutic options and appropriate referral for further reproductive investigation/treatment.

entries.title: Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: PCOS is a leading cause of oligomenorrhea/anovulation covered by objective 56-1's differential, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: PCOS-related anovulation is a common cause of female-factor infertility under objective 46, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize PCOS using its clinical/diagnostic criteria (oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovarian morphology) and its long-term metabolic implications.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate initial management plan addressing menstrual regulation, fertility goals, and metabolic risk.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Endocrinology (E, completed), which may cover the hyperandrogenism/insulin-resistance mechanism in more depth; GY's content is the menstrual/reproductive presentation and fertility angle. PRIMARY_OWNER not finalized here - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 113 is an exact match: 'Given a patient who presents with vaginal discharge or vulvar pruritus, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications... In particular, the candidate will distinguish sexually transmitted infection (STI) from other causes of vaginal discharge or vulvar pruritus.'

testable_competencies.differential: Distinguish physiologic discharge from infectious vulvovaginitis (e.g., candidiasis, bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis) and from STI causes.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate appropriate diagnostic testing and first-line management.

entries.title: Sexually Transmitted Infections (Gynecologic Presentation)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 113's key objective explicitly requires distinguishing STI from other causes of vaginal discharge/vulvar pruritus, making STI recognition and management a directly named component of this objective.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_management: Recognize common gynecologic STI presentations (chlamydia, gonorrhea, trichomoniasis), initiate appropriate testing and treatment, and address partner notification/reportability.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Infectious Diseases and Public Health and Preventive Medicine (both not yet mapped), which may cover reportable-disease/partner-notification obligations in more depth; PRIMARY_OWNER not finalized here - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

entries.title: Bartholin Gland Abscess

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a Bartholin gland abscess as a cause of unilateral vulvar swelling/pain and identify indications for drainage/marsupialization vs. conservative management.

entries.zero_question_reason: No confirmed MCC evidence; retained as a distinct unit only because Toronto Notes gives it independent topic status, per project convention (see GM-08 Immobility precedent).
entries.uncertain_reason: No MCC objective specifically addresses Bartholin gland abscess or vulvar abscess; the closest candidates (Pelvic pain, Abdominal/pelvic masses) describe a different anatomic presentation and were not used as evidence to avoid overreach.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 73 explicitly requires identifying patients with acute pelvic pain caused by a life-threatening condition; PID (and its complication, tubo-ovarian abscess) is a key cause covered by this requirement, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: PID typically arises from an ascending STI/cervicitis captured under objective 113's STI-differentiation requirement, though PID itself is not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_management: Recognize PID from its clinical presentation (pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness, discharge, fever), initiate empiric antibiotic treatment, and identify indications for hospitalization or drainage of tubo-ovarian abscess.
testable_competencies.complications: Recognize long-term complications (infertility, chronic pelvic pain, ectopic pregnancy risk) as counselling points.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 9-2 requires diagnosing the cause of shock and recognizing urgency; toxic shock syndrome is a distinct shock etiology (often tampon/foreign-body-associated) covered by this general requirement, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize toxic shock syndrome as a cause of shock in a gynecologic context (tampon use, postpartum, surgical site), identify the source, and initiate urgent resuscitation and source control.

entries.title: Gynecologic Surgical Site Infections

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize postoperative infection following a gynecologic procedure (e.g., post-hysterectomy cuff cellulitis/abscess) and initiate appropriate management or referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps General and Thoracic Surgery (GS, completed), which covers general surgical-site infection management; GY's distinct content (if any) would be gynecologic-procedure-specific risk factors. PRIMARY_OWNER not finalized here - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.
entries.zero_question_reason: General surgical-site infection recognition and management is already represented by SU-GS-08; this record retains only the gynecologic procedural context pending ownership adjudication.

entries.title: Sexual Abuse and Assault

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 114-3's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Sexual abuse/exploitation (sex trafficking)' as a component of adult abuse; this unit's forensic/safety-oriented gynecologic content (examination, evidence collection, reporting, safety planning) is the gynecologic-encounter operationalization of that broader abuse-recognition objective, though 114-3 is not gynecology-specific and does not name examination/evidence-collection procedure in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_response: Recognize disclosure or clinical findings suggestive of sexual abuse/assault, assess immediate safety and forensic considerations, and initiate an appropriate examination, reporting, and support/referral plan.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Mandatory-reporting and forensic-examination protocols are provincially/territorially administered in Canada and may also be covered by ELOM in more general consent/reporting terms; content here is kept to the gynecologic clinical-encounter angle. PRIMARY_OWNER/DISTINCT_CONTEXT not finalized here - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit per section 9's guidance that pregnancy/reproductive-context reasoning may later justify DISTINCT_CONTEXT.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 94 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with sexual dysfunction or disorder, the candidate will address the issues and offer appropriate support and management measures.'

testable_competencies.assessment: Address a patient's sexual dysfunction (e.g., dyspareunia, low desire, arousal or orgasmic disorder) in an unbiased, nonjudgmental way, identifying contributing physical and psychosocial factors.
testable_competencies.management: Offer appropriate initial support and management measures or referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 57 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with physiological menopause, the candidate will be able to explain and prevent the undesirable effects of menopause.'

testable_competencies.counselling: Explain the physiology and expected symptoms of menopause and counsel on prevention/management of its undesirable effects (vasomotor symptoms, bone/cardiovascular risk, genitourinary syndrome).

entries.title: Menopause Hormone Therapy

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 57's 'explain and prevent undesirable effects of menopause' requirement encompasses hormone therapy as the primary intervention for vasomotor symptoms, though the objective text does not itself specify hormone-therapy risk/benefit detail.

testable_competencies.risk_benefit_counselling: Recognize the indications, contraindications, and major risk/benefit considerations for menopause hormone therapy at a level sufficient to counsel and initiate referral, without reference to a specific current regimen.

do_not_test: Specific current hormone-therapy formulation, dose, or regimen recommendations - encoded during question-generation source research, not at this scope stage, per project accuracy rules on changing treatment recommendations.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 83 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with prolapse/pelvic floor relaxation, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications, and will initiate an appropriate management plan.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose and stage pelvic organ prolapse (cystocele, rectocele, uterine/vault prolapse) and identify contributing risk factors.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate management plan (conservative vs. pessary vs. surgical referral).

entries.title: Urinary Incontinence (Gynecologic)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 47-2 is an exact match: 'Given an adult patient with urinary incontinence, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications, and initiate an appropriate management plan. In particular, the candidate will address the two most common subtypes of urinary incontinence: stress incontinence and urge incontinence.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate stress from urge urinary incontinence in a female patient and identify pelvic-floor/prolapse contributions.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate management plan (pelvic floor therapy, pharmacologic, or surgical referral).

entries.cross_discipline_note: Objective 47-2 is not gynecology-specific and is shared with Urology (not yet mapped); GY's content is the pelvic-floor/prolapse-associated female presentation. PRIMARY_OWNER not finalized here - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with an abdominal mass or a pelvic mass, the candidate will complete a relevant history and physical examination, and order pertinent investigations to determine the most likely diagnosis... recognize the features of a mass and any associated findings that indicate the need for immediate investigation.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Generate a differential for a pelvic mass by patient age/menopausal status and characterize features (size, laterality, mobility, associated findings) suggesting malignancy.
testable_competencies.urgency: Recognize features indicating need for immediate investigation or referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Endometrial cancer is a leading cause of a uterine/pelvic mass covered by objective 2's differential, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Postmenopausal bleeding, the cardinal presenting symptom of endometrial cancer, falls under objective 112's abnormal-bleeding evaluation requirement, though endometrial cancer is not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize postmenopausal bleeding as the cardinal warning sign of endometrial cancer and identify major risk factors (unopposed estrogen exposure, obesity, PCOS, tamoxifen).
testable_competencies.workup: Initiate appropriate first-line investigation (endometrial biopsy/imaging) and recognize indications for urgent gynecologic-oncology referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Ovarian cancer is a leading cause of a pelvic/adnexal mass covered by objective 2's differential, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the often-nonspecific presenting features of ovarian cancer (bloating, early satiety, pelvic pain, adnexal mass) and identify features suggesting malignancy vs. benign adnexal mass.
testable_competencies.referral: Initiate appropriate investigation (imaging, tumour markers) and recognize indications for gynecologic-oncology referral.

entries.title: Cervical Cancer and Cervical Cancer Screening

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74 covers periodic preventive health advice broadly; cervical cancer screening (Pap/HPV testing per current Canadian guidance) is a component of this preventive-health-encounter competency, though objective 74's retrieved excerpt does not name cervical screening specifically.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Postcoital and intermenstrual bleeding, key presenting features of cervical cancer, fall under objective 112's abnormal-bleeding evaluation, though cervical cancer is not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.screening: Recognize the population and interval eligible for cervical cancer screening and the appropriate next step for an abnormal screening result.
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize clinical presentations of cervical cancer (postcoital bleeding, abnormal discharge, advanced-stage pelvic symptoms) warranting urgent investigation.

do_not_test: Specific current cervical screening interval, start/stop age, or HPV-vs-Pap testing algorithm - jurisdiction/guideline-dependent and researched source-first at question-generation stage, not encoded at this scope stage.

entries.title: Fallopian Tube Malignancy
entries.zero_question_reason: Primary fallopian tube malignancy is rare and no MCC objective addresses it; generalist-relevant content (presentation as a pelvic mass or abnormal bleeding) is already captured under SU-GY-28 (Pelvic Mass) and SU-GY-06 (Abnormal Uterine Bleeding), so this unit is retained only for source-node accounting, not as an independently tested competency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Vulvar cancer commonly presents with a vulvar lesion and pruritus, overlapping objective 113's vulvar-pruritus presentation, though vulvar malignancy is not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A vulvar mass/lesion is only loosely analogous to the abdominal/pelvic mass presentation named in objective 2; retained as weak supporting context rather than primary evidence.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a persistent vulvar lesion, ulcer, or pruritus unresponsive to first-line treatment as a warning feature requiring biopsy to exclude vulvar malignancy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Primary vaginal cancer is rare and not named in any retrieved MCC objective; abnormal vaginal bleeding (its most common presenting feature) is the nearest adjacent evidence under objective 112.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize abnormal vaginal bleeding or a visible vaginal lesion in an at-risk patient (e.g., prior cervical dysplasia, DES exposure) as a rare but important cause requiring biopsy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: GTD classically presents with abnormal vaginal bleeding in pregnancy/post-molar-evacuation, covered by objective 112's differential, though GTD is not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A uterus large-for-dates with a heterogeneous mass is a classic GTD presentation covered by objective 2's differential, though GTD is not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize molar pregnancy (hydatidiform mole) from its classic presentation (markedly elevated beta-hCG, uterus large-for-dates, first-trimester bleeding, hyperemesis) and its malignant sequela (choriocarcinoma).
testable_competencies.management: Initiate appropriate evacuation and beta-hCG surveillance, and recognize indications for oncology referral.

entries.title: Common Gynecologic Medications (Reference)
do_not_test: Reference medication-summary table - drug names/doses/classes are reference material duplicating each condition-specific unit's own management content, not an independent competency.
entries.zero_question_reason: Reference material duplicating condition-unit management content; per project scope rules, exact current treatment recommendations are not encoded at this scope stage.

entries.title: Landmark Gynecology Trials (Reference)
entries.zero_question_reason: Bibliographic/trial-summary reference content, not an independently testable clinical competency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 93-1 requires distinguishing 'normal variation of pubertal development from symptoms of serious underlying disorders'; this unit's normal Tanner-stage sequence is the normal-variation baseline that operationalizes that distinction, though the objective's own title/rationale is scoped to abnormal development.

testable_competencies.normal_staging: Recognize the normal sequence and timing of pubertal stages (Tanner staging, menarche timing) as the baseline for identifying precocious or delayed puberty.

entries.title: Premenstrual Syndrome and Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 56-3 is an exact match covering both conditions together: 'Given a patient with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMS), the candidate will assess the severity and complications... Specifically, the candidate will differentiate PMS from normal premenstrual symptoms or from other causes of physical and mood changes.'

testable_competencies.differential: Differentiate normal premenstrual symptoms from PMS and from PMDD, and from other causes of cyclical physical/mood changes.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate management plan and explore the psychosocial impact of the condition.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2's causal_conditions list explicitly names 'leiomyoma' under Gynecologic causes of a pelvic mass: '...Gynecologic (e.g., ovarian cysts, ectopic or normal pregnancy, leiomyoma)'. Fibroids (uterine leiomyoma) is a named example within this objective's differential rather than the subject of its own dedicated objective.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Fibroids are a leading structural cause of heavy/abnormal menstrual bleeding, which objective 112 covers; the objective's causal_conditions list 'benign growths' generically under intermenstrual/menorrhagia causes rather than naming fibroids/leiomyoma explicitly.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize fibroids (uterine leiomyoma) as a common benign cause of a pelvic/uterine mass and of heavy or abnormal uterine bleeding, and identify major epidemiologic risk factors (age, Black patients affected earlier/more severely).
testable_competencies.management: Initiate an appropriate management plan across the medical-to-surgical spectrum (GnRH agonist/antagonist therapy, uterine artery embolization, myomectomy, hysterectomy) based on bleeding vs. bulk symptoms and fertility goals.
